content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp with crab stuffing is a seafood dish where large peeled shrimp are filled with a mixture of crab meat, spices, and sometimes creamy cheese. The product is usually steamed, baked, or pan‑fried, resulting in a tender shrimp with a flavorful, aromatic filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are one of the most widely consumed seafoods worldwide.
Crab meat is rich in protein and trace minerals such as zinc and copper.
Stuffed shrimp are a traditional appetizer in Asian cuisines, especially Japanese and Chinese.
The stuffing often combines crab meat, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and seasonings for a creamy texture.
These bites are commonly served as a starter in seafood restaurants.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Both shrimp and crab provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, stuffed shrimp contain relatively little saturated fat.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood supplies polyunsaturated fats that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Rich in minerals and vitamins
items.content: Crab meat is high in zinc, copper and vitamin B12, while shrimp are good sources of selenium and vitamin D.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Selenium and zinc found in the product help maintain normal immune function.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp and crab can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Seafood contains cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Certain seafood may contain heavy metals or toxins if not properly sourced and processed.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: When soy sauce or added salt is used in the stuffing, the sodium content can be high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stuffed shrimp can be served hot as an appetizer, added to salads, pasta, or rice dishes. They are also convenient on skewers, quickly pan‑seared to a golden crust. Garnish with lemon wedges and fresh herbs for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared shrimp with crab stuffing in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a sealed bag – they retain quality for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
